commit_subject: (screen-flagged) Regenerate of existing 164(f) module changes entity TaxUnit -> Person, re-anchors imports from us:statutes/26/1401#self_employment_oasdi_tax / #self_employment_hospital_insurance_tax to us:statutes/26/1401/a#old_age_survivors_and_disability_insurance_tax and us:statutes/26/1401/b/1#self_employment_income_tax, adds proof spans, and rewrites the companion test.
description: Replace parent 1401 tax imports with child 1401(a) OASDI and 1401(b)(1) Medicare SECA imports.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: 26 USC 164(f)(1) allows the half-of-SECA deduction "In the case of an individual" against taxes section 1401 imposes "on the self-employment income of every individual", but the pre-fix module encoded both derived rules at entity TaxUnit and drew their SECA amounts from the household-scoped parent 1401 module, so the deduction was computed once per tax unit on an aggregate, uncapped base rather than per individual.
triage.triage_notes: Statute text read through the pinned corpus release (resolve_provision on us/statute/26/164) and confirms the operative phrase "In the case of an individual"; the new import targets statutes/26/1401/a.yaml and statutes/26/1401/b/1.yaml were read at this commit and are both entity: Person, while the old target statutes/26/1401.yaml (still present at both parent and commit) is entity: TaxUnit throughout. Three real changes land together in this one module and I had to pick one kind: (a) entity TaxUnit -> Person, chosen as decisive because the source phrase settles it; (b) the import re-anchoring from the parent 1401 module onto the 1401(a)/1401(b)(1) children, which could equally be read as untraceable_branch (formula grounded on a coarser/stale provision module); (c) the amount consequence -- the companion test expectation moved 7650 -> 7064.775, i.e. 0.5*0.153*100000 versus 0.5*0.153*(0.9235*100000), because the new chain routes through 1402(a)/(b) net earnings and the section 230 contribution-and-benefit base, which the old parent 1401 module ignored (it multiplied a raw self_employment_income input by the rates). The encoder run root is named "164-f-seca-wage-base-v8", which supports the SECA-base motivation. The 'other than the taxes imposed by section 1401(b)(2)' carve-out was already correctly represented pre-fix (additional Medicare tax was never summed), so this is not an unrepresented_clause. Non-fidelity noise in the same diff: proof spans added, import hashes updated, block-style YAML reflowed to flow style, the third rule's local sha256:local import proof atom dropped, and the module summary regressed to a typo ("In the case of an an individual") while dropping the "(1) In general" heading. No PR reviews or comments exist on PR #60 (reviews, review_comments, issue_comments all empty) and the commit body is empty, so the defect is evidenced by the diff plus the statute rather than named by a maintainer; the PR body's "Keep the deduction person-scoped" reads as a description of the result, not an admission that the prior encoding was TaxUnit-scoped, which is why confidence is below 0.8. PR body also notes a 32(c)(2) regeneration in the same effort was blocked and is not in this commit.
triage.verifier_justification: The pinned corpus text of 26 USC 164(f)(1) reads "In the case of an individual ... an amount equal to one-half of the taxes imposed by section 1401", and section 1401 imposes its tax "on the self-employment income of every individual", so the deduction is per-individual; the pre-fix module declared both derived rules at `entity: TaxUnit` and drew their SECA components from the parent `statutes/26/1401.yaml` rules `self_employment_oasdi_tax` / `self_employment_hospital_insurance_tax`, which I confirmed are themselves `entity: TaxUnit` and are computed on an aggregate `taxable_self_employment_income_for_section_1401` with no per-person contribution base. The fix changes both rules to `entity: Person` and re-anchors the imports to `us:statutes/26/1401/a#old_age_survivors_and_disability_insurance_tax` and `us:statutes/26/1401/b/1#self_employment_income_tax`, which are `entity: Person` and run off 1402(a)/1402(b) per-individual net earnings and the section 230 contribution base — the companion test expectation moves 7650 -> 7064.775 accordingly. That is a change to the encoded entity, population and input surface, not bookkeeping, and no competing kind fits better: the 1/2 parameter, the 1401(b)(2) carve-out, the `if taxpayer_is_individual ... else: 0` logic, and the 1990-01-01 effective date are all unchanged, and the pre-fix formula was grounded on the correct provision (section 1401) merely at the wrong scope, so untraceable_branch and amount_mismatch do not apply.
triage.verifier_notes: Two corrections to the first reader's write-up, neither of which changes the kind: (1) the parent 1401 module's rules are TaxUnit-scoped, not "household-scoped" — verified at eba8177e:statutes/26/1401.yaml, where self_employment_oasdi_tax and self_employment_hospital_insurance_tax both carry `entity: TaxUnit`; (2) the reader's quote is from the PR body's import bullet, which is weaker evidence than the diff, and the same PR body also says "Keep the deduction person-scoped", which mischaracterizes its own change since the diff plainly flips `entity: TaxUnit` -> `entity: Person` on both derived rules. A better quote is the entity line itself. The pre-fix base also lacked 1402(a)'s net-earnings reduction and 1402(b)'s cap (hence 7650 vs 7064.775 in the test), but that defect lives in statutes/26/1401.yaml; 164/f.yaml's own defect is the entity and the import scope. Remaining diff content is cosmetic or provenance: added proof spans, YAML reflow from block scalars to flow style, removal of the `sha256:local` self-import proof atom, and a new "an an individual" typo plus a dropped "(1) In general" in the module summary — the summary typo is worth a reviewer note as a regeneration-quality nit, not a fidelity issue.
